summary: CobaltFin production streaming blackout: session-resume failures, truncated transcripts, and urgent enterprise escalation
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-08 01:02 and 01:28 UTC CobaltFin reported a region-wide streaming blackout in us-west-2. Users saw immediate streaming disconnects, failed session resume attempts, and truncated transcripts. The customer observed duplicate partial completions for some requests and a spike in billed tokens tied to repeated retries. Impact: Production traffic for CobaltFin (enterprise, dedicated plan) experienced degraded UX and SLA breaches for 26 minutes. Some requests were retried by client-side logic leading to billing overage exposure and a high-severity customer escalation. Environment: prod - us-west-2, dedicated pool df-7g-03, model variants rw-open-13b-v1 and rw-quant-13b-ff16. Steps to reproduce: 1) Heavy burst of requests (~2.8x normal) to /v1/streams endpoint with session-affinity headers. 2) During autoscaler activity and rolling kernel selection, several streaming workers restarted. 3) Clients attempted session-resume; some resumed successfully, others received EOF or truncated event streams. Logs: See attached excerpts from streaming-proxy (streaming-proxy-logs-03-08.log), session-coordinator events, and billing-usage snapshots during the window. Error patterns: transport EOF, session-state-mismatch, partial-completion-ack. Customer expectation: full replayable transcripts or clear error with idempotency token to prevent duplicated billing and duplicates in downstream systems.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: autoscaler triggered worker restarts during kernel-selection after a quantized variant rollout. Observed: autoscaler started new nodes at 01:01:50 UTC, and a rolling kernel update (related PR) began at 01:02:05. At 01:02:12 multiple stream-proxy instances closed active streams while their L7 proxy rebalanced connections. Session-coordinator showed stale affinity mappings for 18% of sessions because KV prefix heartbeat lagged during node handoff. This caused some clients to open new sessions without valid continuation tokens, leading to truncated transcripts and duplicate partial completions. Billing telemetry showed repeated request retries from CobaltFin's client over the recovery window. Root cause: combination of concurrent kernel-selection rollout + autoscale events exposing a race in session handoff path. Mitigations during incident: 1) temporarily disabled rolling kernel selection for ded-pool df-7g-03. 2) increased session-coordinator heartbeat frequency for the pool. 3) applied a hotfix to stream-proxy to queue graceful drain instead of closing streams immediately. Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1427 addresses graceful drain ordering.

resolution: Applied immediate mitigations (rollback of kernel selection, stream-proxy hotfix, increased heartbeat). Issued billing credit to CobaltFin (15% of affected window). Monitored stability for 72 hours; no recurrence observed. Ticket closed after post-incident review and action items scheduled for engineering backlog.
